standard.title: Develop project plans for time, cost, risk and production
standard.description: develop project plans for intended purposes and audiences to individually and collaboratively manage projects, taking into consideration time, cost, risk, processes and production of designed solutions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can develop project plans to individually and collaboratively manage time, cost and production (AC9TDE8P05). They have experience with sequencing and tracking tasks. They have not yet developed plans for specific intended purposes and audiences, incorporated formal risk and contingency planning, or investigated manufacturing process strategies for production enhancement.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop project plans for intended purposes and audiences that manage time, cost, risk, processes and production of designed solutions — including flowcharts, spreadsheets, equitable role distribution, contingencies, and production enhancement strategies.

nodes.label: Planning and interpreting production timelines
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can produce, explain and interpret drawings and production timelines using digital tools for a design project.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a production timeline using a digital tool; include at least three tasks with timeframes and dependencies; explain one dependency between tasks.
nodes.typical_width: Produce and interpret production timelines and flowcharts using digital tools (spreadsheets, planning software); include task dependencies, resource requirements and sequencing logic; explain how the timeline supports efficient, safe and sustainable workflows.
wider: Create a production flowchart that maps all decision points in a production process — explain how the flowchart identifies where safety checks, quality reviews or sustainability decisions occur
Produce a materials and equipment needs analysis using a spreadsheet — calculate quantities, costs and sourcing requirements for the production plan
Compare two approaches to sequencing the same production tasks — explain which produces a more efficient workflow and why

response_modes.reason: Production timeline creation requires precision — task sequence, dependencies, durations and milestones must be specific enough to be actionable. Students who produce vague plans cannot use them for collaboration or risk identification.

success_criteria: Production plan is produced using a digital tool with at least three sequenced tasks
At least one task dependency is identified and explained
nodes.hinge_reason: A production plan that cannot be interpreted by collaborators makes N2 equitable role distribution impossible — if the timeline and task structure are unclear, team members cannot negotiate distribution or identify their responsibilities.

nodes.label: Collaborative planning with equitable role distribution
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can collaboratively develop a production plan with equitable distribution of roles, tasks and deadlines, including flexibility and contingencies.
nodes.minimum_width: In a collaborative project, assign roles and tasks to all team members with deadlines; identify at least one contingency if a task is delayed or a person is unavailable.
nodes.typical_width: Collaboratively develop a production plan that distributes work equitably — assign roles and tasks based on skills and availability; discuss and agree on deadlines and flexibility; build contingencies for foreseeable risks; monitor and adjust the plan as the project progresses.
wider: Reflect on the equity of role distribution in a completed collaborative project — evaluate whether the plan achieved equitable contribution and what changes would improve future plans
Develop a contingency plan that addresses at least three distinct risks (material, personnel, timeline) — test the contingency plan by simulating a specific risk event
Investigate how professional design and manufacturing teams structure equitable collaboration — identify what practices could be applied to student projects
success_criteria: All team members have assigned roles and tasks in the plan
At least one contingency is documented for an identified risk

nodes.label: Strategies to enhance production
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate manufacturing processes to identify strategies that enhance production — reducing waste, cutting costs, speeding up processes or forming beneficial production partnerships.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one strategy to enhance a production process; explain what it reduces or improves and why.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate manufacturing processes to identify multiple production enhancement strategies — waste reduction, cost reduction, speed improvement, process optimisation or beneficial partnerships; evaluate each strategy for its practical applicability to the design project; incorporate selected strategies into the project plan.
wider: Investigate lean manufacturing or similar production improvement frameworks — identify which principles apply to the design project and explain how they would change the production plan
Identify where in the production process beneficial partnerships (e.g. with specialist manufacturers, suppliers or fabricators) could reduce cost, time or complexity — evaluate the trade-offs
Map production waste at each stage of a design project and identify reduction strategies — evaluate the sustainability benefit of each strategy

response_modes.reason: Production enhancement requires students to reason from current process → identify inefficiency or waste → identify strategy → evaluate applicability. Without this structure, students suggest generic improvements without analysing whether they apply to their specific production context.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one production enhancement strategy that is specific to the design project
Explains what it improves and how it would be implemented — not just names the strategy
